note: Class: rival account of how faith relates to evidence (WF-N). Recognizability of a revelation by external signs, the motives of credibility, is a correctness condition answering to reason shared with outsiders, which the cut-off thesis excludes for every correct religious move. Defeated as a description of the Catholic practice only conditionally: WF-FAILS-AS-DESCRIPTION-OF-CATHOLIC-PRACTICE derives that the fideist pair fails from three open premises (the stated Dei Filius canon, the open definition bridge and the open shared-reason reading), so under #999 it counts as no refutation. Minimalism (STMT-MINIMALISM-ALLOWS-EXTERNAL-EVIDENCE) does not hold the cut-off thesis and is not a rival here. No refutes relation.
